column1: # Every way a request can fail, and what each surface calls it. The command,
# the C module and the Go module each word their own messages; this is what
# keeps them saying the same thing. Tests on both sides read it.
# Tab-separated. Lines starting with '#' are comments; blank lines are ignored.
# refusal   a label, for test output
# code      the C module's return code, from zuid.h
# c         its name in zuid.h
# go        the Go module's Err value that errors.Is matches, '-' for none
# zig       the core's error names, comma-separated, '-' for none
# surfaces  which of go, c and cli word this one themselves, comma-separated,
#           '-' for none
# phrase    what each of those surfaces' messages has to contain, ignoring
#           case. ' ... ' between two parts means anything can come between
#           them, in that order.
# Every core error and every code in zuid.h has a row. Codes 3 and 11 are
# retired and stay that way.
# Not every surface words every failure:
#   unknown-base   C hands back the conversion library's own text, and Go
#                  wraps it. Both still say "unknown base".
#   convert        the library's own words, passed through everywhere
#   buffer         C's out buffer and the command's own size cap are two
#                  different limits, and Go has neither
#   hash-too-wide  the command has no hash width flag
#   env            Go names the cause it ran into instead, such as an empty
#                  host name or a random source that ran dry. A clock that
#                  cannot be read is also code 10, and C and the command both
#                  say "the system clock could not be read" for it.
